title: With Due Respect (Vol. 7) -- Ch. 8: Meek and Humble of Heart
keywords: whoever exalts himself will be humbled
primary_topics: Chapter 8 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7) -- CJP's August 24, 2008 Inquirer column reproducing his eulogy for Patricio 'Pat' Garcia (lawyer, CPA and Inquirer director-treasurer), built around the Gospel phrase 'meek and humble of heart'
How Pat embodied that phrase -- gentle, fair and resolute, yet 'low profile' and 'uneasy when publicly acclaimed,' with 'no hidden agenda... no vile motives'

Pat's quiet kindness toward CJP -- introducing him to the Inquirer (fulfilling a newspaper-boy's 'impossible dream' of leading the broadsheet), arranging his heart consult in 1996, and publishing his book 'Leveling the Playing Field'
A farewell grounded in faith -- the promise of John 14 that 'where I am, you also shall be' -- and the confidence that the meek and humble Pat is now with the Lord
sub_topics: The occasion: with Pat Garcia 'laid to rest' on August 17, CJP reproduces his eulogy from 'the St. James Church in Ayala Alabang,' opening with Matthew 11:28-30 and its phrase 'meek and humble of heart,' which 'describes exactly what Pat was'

How they met: CJP met Pat (with Ben Pangilinan, introduced by 'the late Mars Quimson' in 1987) as counsel to their 'Excel Group,' and was 'ushered... to the Philippine Daily Inquirer and to Marixi... Prieto,' who 'enticed [him]' to become president of 'the most widely read broadsheet' -- 'fulfilling [his] impossible dream' as 'a poor boy hawking newspapers in the streets of Sampaloc... in the late 1940s and early 1950s'

Pat's character: their business tie 'ended in 1995 when [CJP] joined the Supreme Court,' but the friendship endured 'especially on the golf course'; Pat was 'gentle, genteel, considerate, and always fair,' yet not 'docile' -- 'resolute in his convictions and very diligent,' and 'did not have an exaggerated opinion of himself,' preferring a 'low profile' and feeling 'uneasy when publicly acclaimed'

Loving and kind: 'never boastful or proud,' Pat 'always spoke highly and lovingly' of his wife Cora and children (Mike, Chris, Patrick and Nicky), and 'glowed with paternal pride' over his grandchildren -- exemplifying the Lord's teaching that 'whoever exalts himself will be humbled; but whoever humbles himself will be exalted' (Matthew 23:12)

Quiet eloquence: he 'never used unnecessary rhetoric or highfalutin words,' never convinced 'by arm-twisting' or 'backslapping,' and in 'more than 20 years of friendship' was never heard 'erupt in anger or use foul language' -- his 'eloquence... demonstrated quietly but effectively by his actions,' so 'what you see is what you get with Pat'

Compassionate and caring: 'loyal, compassionate, and caring,' Pat helped friends 'neither counting the cost nor expecting anything in return' -- in April 1996, hearing CJP was 'tentatively diagnosed with blocked heart arteries,' he 'voluntarily scheduled a visit' with his cousin, surgeon Dr. Jorge Garcia (the angiogram later showing no bypass was needed)

A patron of his book: in 2004 Pat 'caused the publication by Print Town... of [CJP's] book Leveling the Playing Field and personally took care of its distribution,' so that 'in less than a year, it was sold out'

The farewell: bidding 'adieu,' CJP says he is 'certain that [Pat] is now with our Father in heaven,' invoking the promise of John 14 -- 'where I am, you also shall be' -- and closing that, as one 'who like our Lord was meek and humble of heart,' Pat 'shall be... in the dwelling place prepared for him by our Lord'

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 8 of 'With Due Respect' (Vol. 7), CJP's August 24, 2008 Inquirer column, reproduces his eulogy for Patricio 'Pat' Garcia -- lawyer, CPA and Inquirer director-treasurer -- 'laid to rest' on August 17 and read at 'the St. James Church in Ayala Alabang.' Opening with Matthew 11:28-30, CJP says its phrase 'meek and humble of heart' 'describes exactly what Pat was.' He recalls meeting Pat in 1987 as counsel to the 'Excel Group,' being 'ushered... to the Philippine Daily Inquirer and to Marixi... Prieto,' who 'enticed' him to become president of 'the most widely read broadsheet' -- fulfilling the 'impossible dream' of 'a poor boy hawking newspapers in the streets of Sampaloc.' Though their business tie 'ended in 1995' when CJP joined the Court, the friendship endured 'especially on the golf course.' Pat was 'gentle, genteel... and always fair,' yet 'resolute in his convictions,' kept a 'low profile' and felt 'uneasy when publicly acclaimed,' embodying 'whoever exalts himself will be humbled; but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.' He 'never used... highfalutin words,' was never heard 'erupt in anger,' and let his actions speak, so 'what you see is what you get with Pat.' Loyal and caring, he helped friends 'neither counting the cost nor expecting anything in return' -- in 1996 'voluntarily' arranging CJP's heart consult with his surgeon cousin Dr. Jorge Garcia, and in 2004 having Print Town publish CJP's 'Leveling the Playing Field,' which 'sold out' within a year. Bidding 'adieu,' CJP is 'certain that [Pat] is now with our Father in heaven,' invoking John 14's promise -- 'where I am, you also shall be' -- for one who, 'like our Lord, was meek and humble of heart.'
